reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows Mn-rich oxide formation and Mn depletion zones during oxidation of a different alloy, but none of the passages address Q235 steel, low-temperature annealing (200–300°C), or corrosion behavior in chloride environments. Thus, the key premises about Mn segregation, oxide formation, and corrosion suppression in Q235 steel under the proposed conditions lack direct support.
premises: Mn segregation to grain boundaries and near-surface region can be promoted by thermal annealing in an oxidizing atmosphere in Q235 steel.
A continuous Mn-rich oxide layer can form on the steel surface as a result of this segregation.
This Mn-rich oxide layer can suppress corrosion in harsh chloride environments.
Inert annealing does not significantly alter Mn distribution or corrosion behavior compared to the untreated state.
The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) supports Mn oxidation, segregation, and its role in corrosion protection in relevant contexts.
